# National Geographic Education

> A comprehensive K-12 education platform offering live Explorer Classroom events, interactive resources, and field experiences led by National Geographic explorers and scientists.

National Geographic Education provides engaging, standards-aligned learning experiences that connect students with real explorers, scientists, and storytellers. The platform emphasizes hands-on discovery, conservation biology, environmental resilience, and STEM learning through virtual events and interactive content.

## Key Topics

- Explorer Classroom
- National Geographic Explorers
- Live Events
- K-12 Learning
- STEM Education
- Conservation Biology
- Environmental Science

- Free Educational Resources

## Explorer Classroom Live Events

- [Planet of the Snails and Spiders](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/event/planet-of-the-snails-and-spiders): Live Explorer Classroom event with conservation biologist Martina Panisi on invertebrates for grades 3-8.
- [Life in Hot Water](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/event/life-in-hot-water): Explorer Classroom event with biologist Rosa Vásquez Espinoza on microbes in extreme freshwater environments.
- [Engineering Adventures In Space](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/event/engineering-adventures-in-space): STEM Explorer Classroom event with systems engineer Tracy Drain on space engineering for grades 3-8.
- [Documenting Environmental Resilience in Africa](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/event/documenting-environmental-resilience-in-africa): Earth Day webinar with photo-artist Miora Rajaonary on the Great Green Wall restoration initiative.

## Storytelling Series

- [Stories on Foot](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/event/stories-on-foot): Explorer Classroom storytelling series with journalist Paul Salopek on the Out of Eden Walk journey.
- [Unhidden Voices of History](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/event/unhidden-voices-of-history): Explorer Classroom storytelling workshop with journalist James Edward Mills on overlooked community histories.

## Main Education Hub

- [Education | National Geographic Society](https://education.nationalgeographic.org): National Geographic's main education hub offering live events, maps, videos, and interactive resources for K-12 learning.
